   181	}
   182	rule_implementer_single_session() {
   183	  local ids n sid f bad=""
   184	  ids="$(jq -r '[.phases // [] | .[] | select(.skipped != true and (.name == "PLAN" or .name == "IMPLEMENT" or .name == "FIX")) | .session_id]' "$R/meta/pipeline.json")"
   185	  n="$(jq 'length' <<<"$ids")"
   186	  [[ "$n" -gt 0 ]] || { EVID="no implementer record"; return 1; }
   187	  [[ "$(jq '[.[] | select(. == null)] | length' <<<"$ids")" -eq 0 ]] || { EVID="an implementer record has no session_id"; return 1; }
   188	  [[ "$(jq 'unique | length' <<<"$ids")" -eq 1 ]] || { EVID="implementer session ids $(jq -r 'unique | join(",")' <<<"$ids")"; return 1; }
   189	  sid="$(jq -r '.[0]' <<<"$ids")"
   190	  while IFS= read -r f; do
   191	    case "$(jq -r '.name' "$f")" in PLAN|IMPLEMENT|FIX) ;; *) continue ;; esac
   192	    jq -e '.resume == null' "$f" >/dev/null && continue
   193	    jq -e --arg s "$sid" '.resume == $s and ((.argv | index("--resume")) as $i | $i != null and .argv[$i + 1] == $s)' "$f" >/dev/null \
   194	      || bad="$bad $(jq -r '.label' "$f")"
   195	  done < <(argv_files)
   196	  [[ -z "$bad" ]] || { EVID="continuation argv does not resume $sid:$bad"; return 1; }
   197	  EVID="one session $sid across $n implementer record(s)"
   198	}
   199	rule_gates_separate_sessions() {
   200	  local r a impl
   201	  r="$(jq -r '[.phases // [] | .[] | select(.name == "REVIEW" and .skipped != true) | .session_id][0] // "null"' "$R/meta/pipeline.json")"
   202	  a="$(jq -r '[.phases // [] | .[] | select(.name == "AUDIT" and .skipped != true) | .session_id][0] // "null"' "$R/meta/pipeline.json")"
   203	  impl="$(jq -c '[.phases // [] | .[] | select(.name == "PLAN" or .name == "IMPLEMENT" or .name == "FIX") | .session_id | select(. != null)] | unique' "$R/meta/pipeline.json")"
   204	  [[ "$r" != null && "$a" != null ]] || { EVID="gate session ids review=$r audit=$a"; return 1; }
   205	  [[ "$r" != "$a" ]] || { EVID="REVIEW and AUDIT share session $r"; return 1; }
   206	  if jq -e --arg r "$r" --arg a "$a" 'index($r) != null or index($a) != null' <<<"$impl" >/dev/null; then
   207	    EVID="a gate shares an implementer session"; return 1
   208	  fi
   209	  EVID="review $r, audit $a, implementer $(jq -r 'join(",")' <<<"$impl")"

   211	rule_effort_flag_medium() {
   212	  local f n=0 ok=0
   213	  while IFS= read -r f; do
   214	    n=$((n + 1))
   215	    jq -e '(.argv // []) | (index("--effort")) as $i | $i != null and .[$i + 1] == "medium"' "$f" >/dev/null && ok=$((ok + 1))
   216	  done < <(argv_files)
   217	  [[ $n -gt 0 && $ok -eq $n ]] || { EVID="--effort medium on $ok/$n phases"; return 1; }
   218	  EVID="--effort medium on $ok/$n phases"
   219	}
   220	rule_skill_effort_stripped() {
   221	  local f n=0 hit=0
   222	  for f in "$R"/sandbox/.claude/skills/*/SKILL.md; do
   223	    [[ -f "$f" ]] || continue
   224	    n=$((n + 1))
   225	    # the YAML frontmatter only (first line `---` to the next `---`); a body line may say effort:
   226	    awk 'NR == 1 && $0 != "---" {exit} NR > 1 && $0 == "---" {exit} NR > 1 && /^effort:/ {hit = 1; exit} END {exit !hit}' "$f" \
   227	      && hit=$((hit + 1))
   228	  done
   229	  [[ $n -gt 0 ]] || { EVID="no sandbox SKILL.md"; return 1; }
   230	  [[ $hit -eq 0 ]] || { EVID="$hit/$n SKILL.md still carry effort:"; return 1; }
   231	  EVID="skill effort lines stripped $n/$n"
   232	}
   233	rule_integrity_clean() {
   234	  local man="$R/sandbox/.claude/checksums.json" msha out
   235	  if [[ "$(jq -r '.arm_toggles.loa_mount' "$R/meta/pipeline.json")" == false ]]; then
   236	    [[ -e "$R/sandbox/.claude" ]] && { EVID="loa_mount: false but sandbox has .claude/"; return 1; }
   237	    EVID="no mount (loa_mount: false)"; return 0
   238	  fi
   239	  msha="$(jq -r '.arm_evidence.manifest_sha256 // empty' "$R/meta/pipeline.json")"
   240	  [[ -n "$msha" && "$msha" != none ]] || { EVID="no arm_evidence.manifest_sha256"; return 1; }
   241	  [[ -f "$man" ]] && jq -e '.files | type == "object"' "$man" >/dev/null 2>&1 || { EVID="no sandbox .claude/checksums.json files map"; return 1; }
   242	  # one hashlib walk over every manifest entry: "<n> <tampered> <missing> <file-sha> <first problem>"
   243	  out="$(python3 -I -c '
   244	import hashlib, json, os, sys
   245	root, man = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
   246	def sha(p):
   247	    h = hashlib.sha256()
   248	    with open(p, "rb") as f:
   249	        for b in iter(lambda: f.read(1 << 20), b""):
   250	            h.update(b)
   251	    return h.hexdigest()
   252	files = json.load(open(man)).get("files") or {}
   253	bad = missing = 0; first = "-"
   254	for rel, want in sorted(files.items()):
   255	    p = os.path.join(root, rel)
   256	    if not os.path.isfile(p):
   257	        missing += 1; first = first if first != "-" else "missing " + rel
   258	    elif sha(p) != want:
   259	        bad += 1; first = first if first != "-" else "tampered " + rel
   260	print(len(files), bad, missing, sha(man), first)' "$R/sandbox" "$man")" || { EVID="hash walk failed"; return 1; }
   261	  local n bad missing filesha first
   262	  read -r n bad missing filesha first <<<"$out"
   263	  [[ "$n" -gt 0 ]] || { EVID="manifest lists no files"; return 1; }
   264	  if [[ "$bad" -gt 0 || "$missing" -gt 0 ]]; then EVID="$bad tampered, $missing missing of $n ($first)"; return 1; fi
   265	  EVID="$n manifest entries verified; manifest_sha256 ${msha:0:12}"
   266	  [[ "$filesha" == "$msha" ]] && EVID="$EVID (matches checksums.json)"
   267	  return 0
   268	}
   269	rule_applicability_refused() {
   270	  local f="$R/meta/refused.json" a t
   271	  if [[ ! -f "$f" ]]; then
   272	    # a run that was not refused: its task type must be one the arm declares
   273	    t="$(jq -r '.task_type // ""' "$R/meta/pipeline.json")"
   274	    local k=build; [[ "$t" == review-catch ]] && k=review-catch
   275	    if jq -e --arg k "$k" --arg t "$t" '(.task_types // ["all"]) as $tt | ($tt | index("all")) or ($tt | index($k)) or ($tt | index($t))' \
   276	         <<<"$ARM_DEF" >/dev/null; then
   277	      EVID="applicable: $t in task_types $(jq -c '.task_types // null' <<<"$ARM_DEF") (no refusal needed)"; return 0
   278	    fi
   279	    EVID="ran on $t outside task_types $(jq -c '.task_types // null' <<<"$ARM_DEF") without a refusal record"; return 1
   280	  fi
   281	  a="$(jq -r '.arm // ""' "$f")"; t="$(jq -r '.type // ""' "$f")"
   282	  [[ "$a" == "$ARM" && -n "$t" ]] || { EVID="refusal record names arm '$a' type '$t'"; return 1; }
   283	  local kind=build; [[ "$t" == review-catch ]] && kind=review-catch
   284	  if jq -e --arg k "$kind" --arg t "$t" '(.task_types // ["all"]) as $tt | ($tt | index("all")) or ($tt | index($k)) or ($tt | index($t))' \
   285	       <<<"$ARM_DEF" >/dev/null; then
   286	    EVID="arm task_types $(jq -c '.task_types' <<<"$ARM_DEF") include $t, yet the run was refused"; return 1
   287	  fi
   288	  EVID="refused $t (task_types $(jq -c '.task_types // null' <<<"$ARM_DEF"))"
   289	}
   290	
   291	# ---- one run ------------------------------------------------------------------------
   292	check_run() {  # check_run <run-dir> → prints lines; returns 0/1; 2 on usage problems
   293	  R="$1"
   294	  local arm rules rule fails=0 total=0 results='[]' ok
   295	  if [[ -n "$ARM_OPT" ]]; then arm="$ARM_OPT"
   296	  elif [[ -f "$R/meta/arm" ]]; then arm="$(sed -n '1p' "$R/meta/arm" | tr -d '[:space:]')"
   297	  elif [[ -f "$R/meta/refused.json" ]]; then arm="$(jq -r '.arm // ""' "$R/meta/refused.json")"
   298	  else arm="$(jq -r '.arm // ""' "$R/meta/pipeline.json" 2>/dev/null || true)"; fi
   299	  [[ -n "$arm" ]] || { echo "took-effect.sh: no arm for $R" >&2; return 2; }
   300	  ARM="$arm"
   301	  ARM_DEF="$(jq -c --arg a "$arm" '[.arms // [] | .[] | select(.id == $a)][0] // empty' <<<"$SUITE_JSON")"
   302	  [[ -n "$ARM_DEF" ]] || { echo "took-effect.sh: arm $arm is not declared in the suite" >&2; return 2; }
   303	  if [[ "$(jq -r '.absent // false' <<<"$ARM_DEF")" == true ]]; then
   304	    if [[ "$JSON" == true ]]; then jq -nc --arg d "$R" --arg arm "$arm" '{run_dir: $d, arm: $arm, ok: true, absent: true, rules: []}'
   305	    else printf 'arm %s: absent (component-absent; no rules)\n' "$arm"; fi
   306	    return 0
   307	  fi
   308	  if [[ -f "$R/meta/refused.json" ]]; then

   315	  while IFS= read -r rule; do
   316	    [[ -n "$rule" ]] || continue
   317	    total=$((total + 1)); EVID=""
   318	    if declare -F "rule_$rule" >/dev/null; then

   320	    else

   322	    fi
   323	    [[ "$ok" == true ]] || fails=$((fails + 1))

   332	      '{run_dir: $d, arm: $arm, ok: $ok, rules: $rules}'

   334	    printf 'arm %s: OK\n' "$arm"
   335	  else
   336	    printf 'arm %s: FAIL (%d of %d rules)\n' "$arm" "$fails" "$total"
   337	  fi

   342	  [[ -d "$RUN_DIR" ]] || usage "run dir not found: $RUN_DIR"

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# =============================================================================
     3	# validate-suite.sh — cycle-130 ablation task-suite validator (SDD §3.2, DEC-0424)
     4	#
     5	# Checks every task of the ablation-2.0 suite before it is frozen, run or graded.
     6	#
     7	# Usage:
     8	#   validate-suite.sh [--root DIR] [--smoke] [--allow-partial] [--suite-file F]
     9	#
    10	#   --root DIR        suite root (default grimoires/loa/evals/ablation-2.0); the
    11	#                     tasks are <root>/tasks/<id>/task.yaml
    12	#   --smoke           also validate <root>/smoke/<id>/task.yaml (never counted)
    13	#   --allow-partial   skip the four-by-four type count (Sprint 258 state)
    14	#   --suite-file F    suite yaml (default evals/suites/ablation-2.0.yaml): arm ids
    15	#                     for the leakage check, arms' task_types, suite_version
    16	#
    17	# Checks (each violation is one stdout line `<task-id>: <reason>`):
    18	#   1. schema: id (= directory name), schema_version 1, type (feature-build |
    19	#      bug-fix | refactor | review-catch), source {kind, date, fix_commit?,
    20	#      base_commit?, bead?, origin?}, post_cutoff (bool), fixture (dir under the
    21	#      root; null only for review-catch), criterion (agent-facing; no path, file
    22	#      name or test name), success_criterion, test_command (array; null only for
    23	#      review-catch), regression_command (array | null), reference_patch (hidden/…
    24	#      | null; required for bug-fix and feature-build), grader_protected (array of
    25	#      relative paths present in the fixture), structural_check (hidden/… | null;
    26	#      required for refactor), bounds {max_turns{}, timeout_min{}} (phase → positive
    27	#      int), review_catch (null, or {fixture, manifest, labels?} for review-catch,
    28	#      both present), suite_version (= the suite file's), TASK.md present
    29	#   2. counts: four tasks of each type under tasks/ (unless --allow-partial)
    30	#   3. allowlist: test_command[0] and regression_command[0] in python3 | pytest |
    31	#      bats | bash | node | npx
    32	#   4. hidden/manifest.json (build types): {"files": [{src, dest}]}; every src
    33	#      exists under hidden/; every dest is relative, inside the tree, no `..`
    34	#   5. fixture path rule (build types): check_fixture_path_rule from
    35	#      lib/sandbox-mount.sh — no .claude/, CLAUDE.md, .loa.config.yaml, grimoires/
    36	#      or .run/ at the fixture's top level; the reference patch touches none either
    37	#   6. leakage: TASK.md and criterion (the task-brief text is built from these)
    38	#      and every phase prompt under evals/harness/lib/phase-prompts/ contain none
    39	#      of: the string `hidden` (any case), a hidden test file's stem, a defect id
    40	#      of the review manifest, a `D[0-9]{2}-` key, an arm id of the suite file
    41	#   7. suite file: every non-absent arm's task_types are known (all | build |
    42	#      review-catch | feature-build | bug-fix | refactor)
    43	#
    44	# Exit: 0 valid; 1 violations (every one listed); 2 usage / unreadable input.
    45	# Tested by evals/tests/validate-suite.bats.
    46	# =============================================================================
    47	set -euo pipefail
    48	export LC_ALL=C
    49	
    50	SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
    51	REPO_ROOT="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)"
    52	ROOT="$REPO_ROOT/grimoires/loa/evals/ablation-2.0"
    53	SUITE_FILE="$REPO_ROOT/evals/suites/ablation-2.0.yaml"
    54	PROMPTS_DIR="${LOA_EVAL_PHASE_PROMPTS_DIR:-$SCRIPT_DIR/lib/phase-prompts}"
    55	SMOKE=false ALLOW_PARTIAL=false
    56	
    57	usage() { sed -n '2,/^# =====.*$/p' "$0" | sed -n '2,45p' | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//' >&2; exit 2; }
    58	die() { echo "validate-suite: $*" >&2; exit 2; }
    59	
    60	while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
    61	  case "$1" in
    62	    --root) ROOT="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
    63	    --smoke) SMOKE=true; shift ;;
    64	    --allow-partial) ALLOW_PARTIAL=true; shift ;;
    65	    --suite-file) SUITE_FILE="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
    66	    --help|-h) usage ;;
    67	    *) die "unknown option: $1 (see --help)" ;;
    68	  esac
    69	done
    70	[[ -n "$ROOT" && -d "$ROOT" ]] || die "suite root not found: ${ROOT:-<empty>}"
    71	ROOT="$(cd "$ROOT" && pwd)"
    72	[[ -f "$SUITE_FILE" ]] || die "suite file not found: $SUITE_FILE"
    73	for tool in yq jq python3; do command -v "$tool" >/dev/null 2>&1 || die "missing tool: $tool"; done

    75	pushd "$SCRIPT_DIR" >/dev/null
    76	# shellcheck source=lib/sandbox-mount.sh
    77	source ./lib/sandbox-mount.sh
    78	popd >/dev/null
    79	
    80	WORK="$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/validate-suite.XXXXXX")"

    82	yq -o=json '.' "$SUITE_FILE" > "$WORK/suite.json" 2>/dev/null || die "suite file is not valid YAML: $SUITE_FILE"
    83	
    84	# Collect task directories: tasks/* (counted) and smoke/* (with --smoke).

    95	      printf '%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\n' "$group" "$n" "$d" "-" >> "$WORK/tasks.tsv"; continue

    99	    else
   100	      printf '%s\t%s\t%s\t%s\n' "$group" "$n" "$d" "!" >> "$WORK/tasks.tsv"
   101	    fi
   102	  done
   103	done
   104	
   105	# Python does the schema, counts, allowlist, manifest, leakage and suite checks;
   106	# it prints violations, and `FIXTURE\t<id>\t<dir>` lines for the path rule below.
   107	python3 -I - "$WORK/tasks.tsv" "$WORK/suite.json" "$ROOT" "$REPO_ROOT" "$ALLOW_PARTIAL" "$PROMPTS_DIR" > "$WORK/out.txt" <<'PY' || { cat "$WORK/out.txt" >&2 2>/dev/null; die "validator crashed"; }
   108	import json, os, re, sys
   109	
   110	tasks_tsv, suite_json, root, repo, allow_partial, prompts_dir = sys.argv[1:7]
   111	allow_partial = allow_partial == "true"
   112	suite = json.load(open(suite_json))
   113	out = []
   114	def bad(tid, msg): out.append(f"{tid}: {msg}")
   115	
   116	TYPES = ["feature-build", "bug-fix", "refactor", "review-catch"]
   117	BUILD = {"feature-build", "bug-fix", "refactor"}
   118	ALLOW = {"python3", "pytest", "bats", "bash", "node", "npx"}
   119	KNOWN_TASK_TYPES = {"all", "build", "review-catch", "feature-build", "bug-fix", "refactor"}
   120	MOUNT_OWNED = (".claude", "CLAUDE.md", ".loa.config.yaml", "grimoires", ".run")
   121	REQUIRED = ["id", "schema_version", "type", "source", "post_cutoff", "fixture", "criterion",
   122	            "success_criterion", "test_command", "regression_command", "reference_patch",
   123	            "grader_protected", "structural_check", "bounds", "review_catch", "suite_version"]
   124	
   125	arms = [a for a in (suite.get("arms") or []) if isinstance(a, dict)]
   126	arm_ids = sorted({a.get("id") for a in arms if isinstance(a.get("id"), str)})
   127	for a in arms:

   139	def rel_ok(p):

   157	def leak_scan(tid, label, text, stems, defect_ids):

1	# Dockerfile.ablation — container executor image for the cycle-130 component ablation
     2	# (SDD D-4.9 / DEC-0411). Extends Dockerfile.sandbox's pinned base and non-root user
     3	# with the Claude Code CLI, the codex CLI, pytest and bats. It holds NO credentials.
     4	# pipeline-run.sh mounts exactly two host paths: the sandbox read-write at /workspace
     5	# and a per-run writable HOME at /home/evaluser (<run>/meta/home: the codex CLI's
     6	# auth.json/config.toml copies, empty .claude/ and .aws/; the CLI's session store). The
     7	# Bedrock route authenticates from AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK passed in the environment.
     8	# The image's tool versions (below) are the batch's versions: every arm runs here.
     9	#
    10	# Build (no build context is needed; nothing is COPY'd):
    11	#   docker build -t loa-ablation:258 - < evals/harness/Dockerfile.ablation
    12	# Run:
    13	#   evals/harness/pipeline-run.sh --executor container --image loa-ablation:258 …
    14	#   (pipeline-run.sh passes --rm --name --user --network bridge --read-only --tmpfs /tmp
    15	#    --pids-limit 512 --memory 4g --cpus 2 and exactly the two mounts)
    16	#
    17	# Digest pinned 2026-02-11 (same base as Dockerfile.sandbox):
    18	#   docker manifest inspect node:20.11.0-bookworm-slim | jq '.manifests[0].digest'
    19	FROM rust:1-bookworm AS brbuild
    20	RUN cargo install beads_rust --version 0.2.6 --root /opt/br --locked 2>/dev/null || cargo install beads_rust --version 0.2.6 --root /opt/br
    21	
    22	FROM node:20.11.0-bookworm-slim@sha256:8ea90c4f037cc3c2f566eb46c53eaac005129113487eda4090058fe554578104 AS base
    23	
    24	ARG CLAUDE_CODE_VERSION=2.1.299
    25	ARG CODEX_VERSION=0.162.1
    26	ARG PYTEST_VERSION=9.0.2
    27	ARG BATS_VERSION=v1.13.0
    28	
    29	RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    30	    bash \
    31	    git \
    32	    jq \
    33	    python3 \
    34	    python3-pip \
    35	    python3-venv \
    36	    grep \
    37	    diffutils \
    38	    coreutils \
    39	    procps \
    40	    ca-certificates \
    41	    curl \
    42	    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
    43	
    44	# yq (mikefarah/yq) with SHA256 integrity verification (as Dockerfile.sandbox)
    45	ARG YQ_VERSION=v4.40.5
    46	ARG YQ_SHA256_AMD64=0d6aaf1cf44a8d18fbc7ed0ef14f735a8df8d2e314c4cc0f0242d35c0a440c95
    47	ARG YQ_SHA256_ARM64=9431f0fa39a0af03a152d7fe19a86e42e9ff28d503ed4a70598f9261ec944a97
    48	RUN arch=$(dpkg --print-architecture) && \
    49	    case "$arch" in \
    50	      amd64) yq_arch="amd64"; yq_sha256="${YQ_SHA256_AMD64}" ;; \
    51	      arm64) yq_arch="arm64"; yq_sha256="${YQ_SHA256_ARM64}" ;; \
    52	      *) echo "Unsupported architecture: $arch" && exit 1 ;; \
    53	    esac && \
    54	    curl -fsSL "https://github.com/mikefarah/yq/releases/download/${YQ_VERSION}/yq_linux_${yq_arch}" \
    55	      -o /usr/local/bin/yq && \
    56	    echo "${yq_sha256}  /usr/local/bin/yq" | sha256sum -c - && \
    57	    chmod +x /usr/local/bin/yq
    58	
    59	# The two CLIs at the versions the fingerprint pins (exact versions, no ranges).
    60	RUN npm install -g --no-fund --no-audit \
    61	      "@anthropic-ai/claude-code@${CLAUDE_CODE_VERSION}" \
    62	      "@openai/codex@${CODEX_VERSION}" \
    63	    && npm cache clean --force
    64	
    65	# pytest for Python fixtures (bookworm's pip is externally managed)
    66	RUN pip3 install --no-cache-dir --break-system-packages "pytest==${PYTEST_VERSION}"
    67	# cheval's declared dependencies (.claude/adapters/pyproject.toml: dependencies + the `full` extra),
    68	# so the sandbox gates (adversarial-review.sh, flatline-orchestrator.sh) can dispatch (lead, DEC-0482)

    70

    81	RUN groupadd -r evaluser && useradd -r -g evaluser -d /home/evaluser -s /bin/bash evaluser

    83	# materialiser writes the beads opt-out marker (LOA_EVAL_BR_BIN unset/absent), so every arm runs the skills'
    84	# markdown fallback alike (lead, Sprint 258).
    85	RUN mkdir -p /home/evaluser/.aws /home/evaluser/.claude /home/evaluser/.codex /workspace && \
    86	    chown -R evaluser:evaluser /home/evaluser /workspace
    87	
    88	ENV TZ=UTC
    89	ENV LC_ALL=C
    90	ENV HOME=/home/evaluser
    91	ENV NPM_CONFIG_IGNORE_SCRIPTS=true
    92	ENV CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK=1
    93	
    94	USER evaluser
    95	WORKDIR /workspace
    96

   101	    echo "All tools verified"
   102

1	# Dockerfile.ablation — container executor image for the cycle-130 component ablation
     2	# (SDD D-4.9 / DEC-0411). Extends Dockerfile.sandbox's pinned base and non-root user
     3	# with the Claude Code CLI, the codex CLI, pytest and bats. It holds NO credentials.
     4	# pipeline-run.sh mounts exactly two host paths: the sandbox read-write at /workspace
     5	# and a per-run writable HOME at /home/evaluser (<run>/meta/home: the codex CLI's
     6	# auth.json/config.toml copies, empty .claude/ and .aws/; the CLI's session store). The
     7	# Bedrock route authenticates from AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK passed in the environment.
     8	# The image's tool versions (below) are the batch's versions: every arm runs here.
     9	#
    10	# Build (no build context is needed; nothing is COPY'd):
    11	#   docker build -t loa-ablation:258 - < evals/harness/Dockerfile.ablation
    12	# Run:
    13	#   evals/harness/pipeline-run.sh --executor container --image loa-ablation:258 …
    14	#   (pipeline-run.sh passes --rm --name --user --network bridge --read-only --tmpfs /tmp
    15	#    --pids-limit 512 --memory 4g --cpus 2 and exactly the two mounts)
    16	#
    17	# Digest pinned 2026-02-11 (same base as Dockerfile.sandbox):
    18	#   docker manifest inspect node:20.11.0-bookworm-slim | jq '.manifests[0].digest'
    19	FROM rust:1-bookworm AS brbuild
    20	RUN cargo install beads_rust --version 0.2.6 --root /opt/br --locked 2>/dev/null || cargo install beads_rust --version 0.2.6 --root /opt/br
    21	
    22	FROM node:20.11.0-bookworm-slim@sha256:8ea90c4f037cc3c2f566eb46c53eaac005129113487eda4090058fe554578104 AS base
    23	
    24	ARG CLAUDE_CODE_VERSION=2.1.299
    25	ARG CODEX_VERSION=0.162.1
    26	ARG PYTEST_VERSION=9.0.2
    27	ARG BATS_VERSION=v1.13.0
    28	
    29	RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    30	    bash \
    31	    git \
    32	    jq \
    33	    python3 \
    34	    python3-pip \
    35	    python3-venv \
    36	    grep \
    37	    diffutils \
    38	    coreutils \
    39	    procps \
    40	    ca-certificates \
    41	    curl \
    42	    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
    43	
    44	# yq (mikefarah/yq) with SHA256 integrity verification (as Dockerfile.sandbox)
    45	ARG YQ_VERSION=v4.40.5
    46	ARG YQ_SHA256_AMD64=0d6aaf1cf44a8d18fbc7ed0ef14f735a8df8d2e314c4cc0f0242d35c0a440c95
    47	ARG YQ_SHA256_ARM64=9431f0fa39a0af03a152d7fe19a86e42e9ff28d503ed4a70598f9261ec944a97
    48	RUN arch=$(dpkg --print-architecture) && \
    49	    case "$arch" in \
    50	      amd64) yq_arch="amd64"; yq_sha256="${YQ_SHA256_AMD64}" ;; \
    51	      arm64) yq_arch="arm64"; yq_sha256="${YQ_SHA256_ARM64}" ;; \
    52	      *) echo "Unsupported architecture: $arch" && exit 1 ;; \
    53	    esac && \
    54	    curl -fsSL "https://github.com/mikefarah/yq/releases/download/${YQ_VERSION}/yq_linux_${yq_arch}" \
    55	      -o /usr/local/bin/yq && \
    56	    echo "${yq_sha256}  /usr/local/bin/yq" | sha256sum -c - && \
    57	    chmod +x /usr/local/bin/yq
    58	
    59	# The two CLIs at the versions the fingerprint pins (exact versions, no ranges).
    60	RUN npm install -g --no-fund --no-audit \
    61	      "@anthropic-ai/claude-code@${CLAUDE_CODE_VERSION}" \
    62	      "@openai/codex@${CODEX_VERSION}" \
    63	    && npm cache clean --force
    64	
    65	# pytest for Python fixtures (bookworm's pip is externally managed)
    66	RUN pip3 install --no-cache-dir --break-system-packages "pytest==${PYTEST_VERSION}"
    67	# cheval's declared dependencies (.claude/adapters/pyproject.toml: dependencies + the `full` extra),
    68	# so the sandbox gates (adversarial-review.sh, flatline-orchestrator.sh) can dispatch (lead, DEC-0482)
    69	RUN pip3 install --no-cache-dir --break-system-packages "rfc8785>=0.1.4" "jsonschema>=4.21" "pyyaml>=6.0" "httpx[http2]>=0.24.0"
    70	
    71	# bats-core at the pinned tag
    72	RUN git clone --depth 1 --branch "${BATS_VERSION}" https://github.com/bats-core/bats-core.git /tmp/bats-core && \
    73	    /tmp/bats-core/install.sh /usr/local && \
    74	    rm -rf /tmp/bats-core
    75	
    76	# Disable npm lifecycle scripts for anything the agent installs later
    77	RUN npm config set ignore-scripts true
    78	
    79	# Non-root user (as Dockerfile.sandbox). At run time /home/evaluser is replaced by the
    80	# per-run HOME bind mount and the process runs as the host uid (--user).
    81	RUN groupadd -r evaluser && useradd -r -g evaluser -d /home/evaluser -s /bin/bash evaluser
    82	# No beads (br) in the image: beads_rust 0.2.6 is not on crates.io and the host binary needs glibc 2.38+; the sandbox
    83	# materialiser writes the beads opt-out marker (LOA_EVAL_BR_BIN unset/absent), so every arm runs the skills'
    84	# markdown fallback alike (lead, Sprint 258).
    85	RUN mkdir -p /home/evaluser/.aws /home/evaluser/.claude /home/evaluser/.codex /workspace && \
    86	    chown -R evaluser:evaluser /home/evaluser /workspace
    87	
    88	ENV TZ=UTC
    89	ENV LC_ALL=C
    90	ENV HOME=/home/evaluser
    91	ENV NPM_CONFIG_IGNORE_SCRIPTS=true
    92	ENV CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK=1
    93	
    94	USER evaluser
    95	WORKDIR /workspace
    96	
    97	# Health check — every tool the fingerprint names is present
    98	RUN bash --version && git --version && jq --version && node --version && \
    99	    python3 --version && python3 -m pytest --version && yq --version && \
   100	    bats --version && claude --version && codex --version && \
   101	    echo "All tools verified"
   102	
   103	ENTRYPOINT []
   104	CMD ["/bin/bash"]

====
     1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# =============================================================================
     3	# pipeline-run.sh — the cycle-130 ablation pipeline executor (SDD §1.4 D-4.1 … D-4.10, §5.6)
     4	#
     5	# Runs ONE task under ONE arm: materialises a sandbox repository (the task's
     6	# fixture tree, or the review-catch PR under pr/, plus the Loa mount from the
     7	# pinned --source-tree), then drives Loa's phases as separate `claude -p`
     8	# sessions inside it, records every phase, enforces the per-run cap and writes
     9	# meta/pipeline.json. One executor serves every task type (D-4.1):
    10	#   review-catch                      REVIEW → AUDIT
    11	#   bug-fix | refactor | feature-build PLAN → IMPLEMENT → REVIEW → FIX? → AUDIT → FIX?
    12	# A FIX runs only when the gate before it wrote a CHANGES_REQUIRED LOA-VERDICT
    13	# trailer (the last `<!-- LOA-VERDICT {…} -->` line of
    14	# grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-1/engineer-feedback.md resp. auditor-sprint-feedback.md);
    15	# a FIX that does not run is recorded `skipped: true`.
    16	# Arms edit the phase set (D-4.2): `sprint_plan: false` drops PLAN; `gates: false`
    17	# ends after IMPLEMENT; `loa_mount: false` runs one BARE session (no mount);
    18	# `flatline: false` keeps PLAN with the Flatline step off; `context_resets: false`
    19	# runs PLAN, IMPLEMENT and FIX as ONE implementer session (`--resume <session_id>`
    20	# from the first session's system/init event) while REVIEW and AUDIT stay separate.
    21	# The suite's `phase_sets[<review-catch|build>]` and an arm's `phases` override the
    22	# default phase list; the toggle edits above apply on top.
    23	#
    24	# Usage:
    25	#   pipeline-run.sh --task-yaml F --arm ID --run-dir D --run-id R --trial N \
    26	#                   --source-tree DIR --suite-file F [--max-run-usd 12] \
    27	#                   [--executor container|host] [--image IMG] [--claude-bin B] \
    28	#                   [--docker-bin D] [--phase-models JSON] [--phase-timeouts JSON] [--dry-run]
    29	#
    30	# Options:
    31	#   --task-yaml F       task.yaml (SDD §3.2); its directory holds TASK.md
    32	#   --arm ID            arm id declared in the suite file (`arms[].id`)
    33	#   --run-dir D         run directory to create (must not exist or be empty);
    34	#                       alias --workspace
    35	#   --run-id R          run id recorded in pipeline.json
    36	#   --trial N           trial number
    37	#   --source-tree DIR   the pinned Loa tree the mount is copied from
    38	#   --suite-file F      evals/suites/ablation-2.0.yaml (read with yq -o=json)
    39	#   --max-run-usd USD   per-run cap (default 12; config evals.ablation.run_cap_usd)
    40	#   --executor MODE     container (default; DEC-0411) or host
    41	#   --image IMG         container image (default loa-ablation:258)
    42	#   --claude-bin B      host-mode CLI (default $EVAL_CLAUDE_BIN, else claude)
    43	#   --docker-bin D      docker CLI (default $EVAL_DOCKER_BIN, else docker)
    44	#   --phase-models JSON {"PLAN": "<model id>", …} override ($LOA_EVAL_PHASE_MODELS)
    45	#   --phase-timeouts JSON {"IMPLEMENT": <seconds>, …} override
    46	#   --dry-run           print the phase plan and exit 0; nothing is created
    47	#
    48	# Run directory layout (DEC-0413 — the grader never reads meta/):
    49	#   sandbox/     the agent's tree (its own .git initialised at `base`)
    50	#   snapshots/   <label>.bundle + index.json ({IMPLEMENT|FIX1|FIX2: commit}) after
    51	#                IMPLEMENT and each FIX
    52	#   transcripts/ events-<label>.jsonl (stream-json), stderr-<label>.log
    53	#   eval/        model-invoke.jsonl, cost-ledger.jsonl (copied out of
    54	#                sandbox/.eval/ after every phase), adversarial-*.json
    55	#   meta/        pipeline.json, phase-<label>.argv.json (argv + captured env),
    56	#                prompt-<label>.md, arm, arm-evidence.txt, arm-env, refused.json,
    57	#                home/ (container mode: the per-run HOME; deleted at exit)
    58	#
    59	# Session (D-4.3, DEC-0394 as amended, DEC-0412): `claude -p <prompt> --output-format
    60	# stream-json --verbose --model <id> --permission-mode bypassPermissions
    61	# --dangerously-skip-permissions --setting-sources project --tools <list>
    62	# --max-turns <cap> [--effort <v>] [--resume <id>]`, cwd sandbox/, with exactly this
    63	# environment: PATH HOME LANG LC_ALL TERM TMPDIR CLAUDE_CODE_USE_BEDROCK
    64	# CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL LOA_MODELINV_LOG_PATH LOA_COST_LEDGER_PATH
    65	# GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1 GH_CONFIG_DIR=<sandbox/.eval/gh-empty>,
    66	# the Bedrock route's pass-through keys when set in the driver's environment
    67	# (AWS_REGION AWS_DEFAULT_REGION AWS_PROFILE AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK
    68	# ANTHROPIC_BEDROCK_REGION_PREFIX ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_{OPUS,SONNET,HAIKU}_MODEL), and the
    69	# arm's LOA_* variables (LOA_ADVERSARIAL_REVIEW_ENFORCE=false for gates: false).
    70	# A python3 -I exec shim closes every descriptor above 2 and keeps exactly those keys;
    71	# values reach it through the environment, never argv, so AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK
    72	# appears in no argv, capture or log (phase-<label>.argv.json records it as "<set>").
    73	# `timeout --signal=TERM --kill-after=15` bounds the CLI.
    74	# Container mode (D-4.9, DEC-0411 as amended) runs the same command inside
    75	#   docker run --rm --name <n> --user <uid>:<gid> --network bridge --read-only
    76	#     --tmpfs /tmp:rw,size=1g --pids-limit 512 --memory 4g --cpus 2
    77	#     -v <run>/sandbox:/workspace:rw -v <run>/meta/home:/home/evaluser:rw
    78	#     -w /workspace -e <KEY=value…> -e AWS_BEARER_TOKEN_BEDROCK <image> python3 -I -c <shim> … claude …
    79	# Exactly two mounts. meta/home/ (mode 0700) holds copies of $HOME/.codex/{auth.json,
    80	# config.toml} when present and empty .claude/ and .aws/; the CLI's session store
    81	# lives there for the whole run, so A6's --resume works across phases. No ~/.claude
    82	# file is ever copied. The directory is deleted at exit and on interrupt.
    83	# image_digest = the image's RepoDigest or id (container), else the fingerprint (host).
    84	# Versions: `fingerprint` is computed from the HOST toolchain; in container mode the
    85	# toolchain that runs the phases is the image's (Claude Code 2.1.299, codex 0.137.0 by
    86	# Dockerfile.ablation), so image_digest identifies the batch's versions. On 2026-10-15
    87	# the host CLI was 2.1.300 while the image pins 2.1.299; every arm runs in the container.
    88	#
    89	# Cap and watchdog (D-4.6, D-4.10): while a phase runs the driver re-prices the
    90	# stream's assistant-turn usage every $LOA_EVAL_WATCHDOG_POLL_S seconds (default 1)
    91	# from per-token prices fetched once per model (pricing.py; $LOA_EVAL_PRICING_JSON
    92	# overrides) and SIGTERMs the phase when spent + estimate ≥ the cap (cap_turn
    93	# recorded). After each phase the result's total_cost_usd (authoritative) plus the
    94	# sandbox cost-ledger rows written during the phase are added; ≥ cap → cap_failure.
    95	#
    96	# Exit codes:
    97	#   0  finished (any verdict)                                   status completed
    98	#   1  agent error: a phase exited non-zero or timed out        status agent_error
    99	#   2  infrastructure: usage, refused arm/type, mount/toggle failure, CLI/docker
   100	#      or image missing, fixture path rule, leak guard          status infrastructure_error
   101	#   3  cap failure (run stopped at the cap)                     status cap_failure
   102	#   4  interrupted (SIGTERM/SIGINT/SIGHUP to the driver, or a phase killed from
   103	#      outside)                                                 status interrupted
   104	# pipeline.json is written for every exit except usage errors and --dry-run; it is
   105	# rewritten with status `running` after each phase so a SIGKILLed driver leaves a
   106	# record (ablation-row.sh reads `running` as interrupted).
   107	#
   108	# Env: EVAL_CLAUDE_BIN, EVAL_DOCKER_BIN, LOA_EVAL_PHASE_MODELS, LOA_EVAL_PRICING_JSON,
   109	# LOA_EVAL_WATCHDOG_POLL_S, LOA_EVAL_CREDS_HOME (where ~/.codex is read; default $HOME),

--- a/evals/harness/run-arms.sh
+++ b/evals/harness/run-arms.sh
@@ -12,6 +12,24 @@
 #               [--model <id>] [--concurrency 2] [--batch <name>]
 #               [--results-dir evals/results/arms] [--retry-wait <s>]
 #               [--allow-unapproved] [--dry-run]
+#               [--max-usd <usd> [--run-cap <usd>]] [--screen [--screen-tasks N]]
+#
+# Spend cap (cycle-130 FR-2, SDD §5.5): --max-usd stops launching before the
+#   next trial when spent + in_flight × run_cap + est_next > max, where spent =
+#   the executor-reported total_cost_usd of this invocation's completed and
+#   failed rows, run_cap = --run-cap (default evals.ablation.run_cap_usd in
+#   .loa.config.yaml, else 12) reserved per running trial, and est_next = the
+#   mean cost of this arm's completed trials (one task type per recall suite),
+#   else the pooled mean, else the suite's ab.cost_hint (or cost_hint), else 5.0.
+#   While the reservation alone blocks the launch it waits for a running trial;
+#   when spent + est_next > max it cuts: no further launches, running trials
+#   finish, STATUS.json gets cut_reason: max_usd and cut = {reason, spent,
+#   in_flight_reserved, max, trials_launched, at_trial}, state partial, exit 1.

DISS-001 [BLOCKING] voice=gpt-5.5-pro Deleting a tracked System Zone script or hook leaves ACTUAL_COUNT unchanged, so preflight passes the count comparison despite an incomplete installation. The previous filesystem count detected this deletion.
  anchor: .claude/scripts/preflight.sh:run_integrity_checks 
  The integrity check now counts index entries rather than files present on disk. git ls-files continues listing tracked files after they have been deleted from the working tree.

DISS-C-001 [ADVISORY] voice=claude-headless A removed .claude/ guard script in a submodule-mounted repo passes check-loa.sh with 'Integrity verified', weakening the tamper detector the three-zone model relies on.
  anchor: .claude/scripts/check-loa.sh:check_integrity 
  In a submodule mount (.loa/.claude is a directory) the new branch reclassifies every absent manifest path as informational 'not-mounted' whenever the same path exists under .loa/. Because the upstream submodule always contains every manifest path, the 'Missing' failure can never fire in submodule mode. Deleting a linked System Zone file (e.g. a hook or gate script symlink) is now indistinguishable from a by-design unlinked path and no longer fails the check.

DISS-C-002 [ADVISORY] voice=claude-headless Tampered or Missing files are printed but check-loa.sh exits 0 if the exit status is derived from the function's return value.
  anchor: .claude/scripts/check-loa.sh:check_integrity 
  The function previously ended with `[[ "$drift" == "false" ]] && log ...`, so it returned non-zero when drift was detected. The new unconditional `return 0` makes the function always succeed. If any caller (or `set -e` propagation) relied on the return status rather than on a counter maintained by fail(), tamper detection no longer affects the script's exit code.

DISS-C-003 [ADVISORY] voice=claude-headless Cost comparisons across arms that use the codex hop are computed on an unverified rate card and cannot be told apart from confirmed pricing after the fact.
  anchor: .claude/defaults/model-config.yaml:gpt-6.1-sol 
  gpt-6.1-sol pricing is an acknowledged placeholder copied from gpt-5.5, yet it is the rate every codex-headless hop estimate and MODELINV row now resolves to. Ledger rows will carry pricing_source=config with no marker that the rate is provisional, so the ablation cost_usd column and any spend reports mix confirmed and placeholder rates indistinguishably.

  anchor: evals/harness/ablation-row.sh:ROW 
  The row builder copies phase fields name, model_requested and models_used straight from meta/pipeline.json with no defaults, but the script's own --validate requires name:string, model_requested:string and models_used:object. A phase that errored before any model invocation (infrastructure_error, interrupted) or a bare arm that lacks these keys produces a row that --validate rejects, even though the builder exited 0.

DISS-C-005 [ADVISORY] voice=claude-headless Degraded-run filtering in the ablation analysis trusts agent-writable artifacts, so a mis-shaped or tampered envelope hides a degraded gate.
  anchor: evals/harness/ablation-row.sh:envelope 
  The header refuses to take the arm from sandbox/ (DEC-0413) because the agent under test can write there, but degraded, degraded_reason and voices_run are derived from sandbox/grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-1/adversarial-*.json, which the same agent can write or edit. A run can therefore present itself as non-degraded with full voice counts regardless of what the gates actually did.

  printf 'echo a\n' > "$R/.claude/scripts/a.sh"
  printf 'echo c\n' > "$R/.claude/scripts/lib/c.sh"

  printf 'override\n' > "$R/.claude/overrides/o.md"
  printf 'outside\n' > "$R/outside.txt"

  printf 'lock' > "$R/.claude/.run/a.lock"
  printf '{}' > "$R/.claude/node_modules/pkg/index.js"
  git -C "$R" init --quiet

setup() {

  CHECK="$ROOT/.claude/scripts/check-loa.sh"

  # upstream tree inside the submodule path
  mkdir -p "$D/.loa/.claude/lib" "$D/.claude"
  printf 'echo a\n' > "$D/.loa/.claude/a.sh"
  printf 'echo b\n' > "$D/.loa/.claude/b.sh"
  printf 'echo c\n' > "$D/.loa/.claude/lib/c.sh"
  # the mount links a.sh only (b.sh and lib/c.sh are not linked)

  source "$ROOT/.claude/scripts/compat-lib.sh"

  HB="$(sha256_portable "$D/.loa/.claude/b.sh" | cut -d' ' -f1)"

  write_manifest

# Sprint 1 Review Feedback

**Reviewer:** Senior Tech Lead Reviewer Agent
**Date:** 2026-10-22
**Sprint Reference:** grimoires/loa/sprint.md
**Implementation Report:** grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-1/reviewer.md (= `pr/PR.md`)

---

## Overall Assessment

The change under review is `pr/head.diff` (72 files): the #1267 mount-integrity work (tracked-tree manifest generator, CI gate, fresh-mount proof, `check-loa.sh` not-mounted outcome, `preflight.sh` count), the cycle-130 ablation harness (`pipeline-run.sh` executor, `lib/sandbox-mount.sh`, `ablation-row.sh`, `took-effect.sh`, `validate-suite.sh`, `freeze.sh`, `spend.sh`, `fingerprint.sh`, run-arms spend cap and screen mode), `Dockerfile.ablation`, the `ablation-2.0` suite, the `gpt-6.1-sol` catalog entry, and 11 bats files.

The design is careful (trust-boundary sourcing by literal path, secrets never on argv, per-run HOME, leak guards, arm evidence recorded from artefacts rather than agent claims) and the parts I could exercise work: `tools/gen-checksums.sh`, `tools/check-manifest-paths.sh`, the `check-loa.sh` mount-scope cases and `spend.sh` pass their suites (31 of 32 runnable tests; the one miss needs the repository's committed manifest, absent from the PR snapshot).

Three things block the merge:

1. The two new test files `ablation-row.bats` and `took-effect.bats` copy a fixture directory (`evals/tests/fixtures/ablation-runs/runs/`) that the PR does not ship. Every test in both files fails in `setup()`, and the PR's own new CI step runs `bats evals/tests/`.
2. The executor and the row builder assume jq 1.7 semantics (a `$label` variable, `{name, label, …}` shorthand, and `split("\u0000") | .[:-1]` on NUL-joined input). On jq 1.6, which the repository itself names as its floor and which Debian 12 / Ubuntu 22.04 ship, every phase aborts at the argv capture and no row can be built. content.text:
Review complete. The feedback file is written and passes the trailer self-check.

**Verdict: CHANGES_REQUIRED** (3 high, 6 medium, 9 low). Written to `grimoires/loa/a2a/sprint-1/engineer-feedback.md`, with the brief's one-line-per-finding form in `review.md` at the repo root.

**Blocking findings**

- **Shipped tests cannot run.** Both new suites copy `evals/tests/fixtures/ablation-runs/runs/` in their setup, and the PR does not include that directory. All 39 tests in `ablation-row.bats` and `took-effect.bats` fail before any assertion, and the PR's own new CI step runs `bats evals/tests/`.
- **The executor and row builder need jq 1.7.** On jq 1.6, which the repo names as its floor and Debian 12 / Ubuntu 22.04 ship, a `$label` variable in `pipeline-run.sh` is a compile error that aborts every run before the first phase, and the `{name, label, …}` shorthand in `ablation-row.sh` means no row can be built. The NUL-split argv capture also drops its last element on 1.6, so `--effort`, `--resume` and the enforce variable vanish from the took-effect evidence. I reproduced this by running the suites from a scratch copy: 4/52, 1/18 and 15/39 unpatched, then 73/91 after a two-symbol rename, with the remaining 10 all the off-by-one.
- **Committed integrity manifest not regenerated.** The PR adds a CI gate comparing `.claude/checksums.json` against the tracked tree, then changes 17 tracked `.claude/` files without an updated manifest. The gate fails on this PR, and downstream mounts would report those paths as Tampered, the symptom class #1267 set out to fix. Confidence medium, since the snapshot cannot show the upstream manifest.

**Non-blocking observations** cover the preflight count no longer detecting deletions, `Missing` never firing in submodule mode, the took-effect integrity rule accepting a regenerated manifest, host-dependent beads state in container mode, codex credential copies surviving a SIGKILL, workflow path filters that exclude `evals/`, and a dead Docker build stage.

**Cross-model dissent** ran with two voices and 7 findings, none rejected. Five were confirmed and folded in; two were triaged as not defects with the reasoning recorded.

**Not verified:** the `arm-toggles`, `run-arms`, `validate-suite` and `freeze` suites depend on fixtures outside the PR snapshot and were not run.
